families.title: Spring-water jugs
families.rules: A fill goes to capacity; emptying removes all water; a pour continues until the source is empty or the destination is full. No stopping partway. Fill and Empty controls are available only when a spring and drain are provided. Otherwise the supply is sealed: pour only and keep every drop. All goal-reaching paths count; minima are optional replay targets.
families.mathematics: Integer state graphs, conserved quantities, gcd and integer linear combinations; Bézout reachability with a source/drain. The closed three-jug variant adds total-volume conservation; do not transfer the two-jug sufficiency theorem without checking.

instances.title: Make one unit
instances.prompt: Use the 3- and 2-unit jugs to leave exactly 1 unit in either jug.
instances.hint: Fill the large jug, then use the smaller jug as a measuring gap.
instances.insight: A capacity difference produces a new amount.
instances.readiness: Entry: count to 3; recognize full and empty.

instances.title: Save the overflow
instances.prompt: Use the 5- and 3-unit jugs to leave exactly 1 unit in either jug.
instances.hint: The second small jugful will not all fit. Keep what remains.
instances.insight: Two small fills can leave a remainder; a partial receiving jug is useful.
instances.readiness: Explore: count to 5 and remember an intermediate amount.

instances.title: Measure what is missing
instances.prompt: Use the 5- and 3-unit jugs to leave exactly 4 units in either jug.
instances.hint: Save two units in the small jug. How much room is left there?
instances.insight: Use the receiving jug’s free space as a measure; filling the largest jug first is useful.
instances.readiness: Explore: same equipment, different target; reverse the earlier plan.

instances.title: Carry a remainder twice
instances.prompt: Use the 7- and 4-unit jugs to leave exactly 2 units in either jug.
instances.hint: After making three units, use the small jug’s one empty space.
instances.insight: Iterated remainder transfer; progress is not monotone in a jug’s displayed amount.
instances.readiness: Stretch: track intermediate states through two fill-and-transfer rounds.

instances.title: Share the spring water
instances.prompt: All 8 units start in jug A. Share them so A and B each hold 4 and C is empty. Keep every drop.
instances.hint: Keep every drop. The smallest jug can return water to the big one.
instances.insight: Conservation changes the state graph: emptied water must be stored elsewhere.
instances.readiness: Stretch: three containers; no tap or drain, but no new arithmetic.

instances.title: A small amount is a useful tool
instances.prompt: All 10 units start in jug A. Share them so A and B each hold 5 and C is empty. Keep every drop.
instances.hint: Try to save one unit in the small jug before filling the middle jug.
instances.insight: A one-unit buffer lets a later pour remove only two; reuse space, not just water.
instances.readiness: Stretch: coordinate storage and free capacity; a longer consolidation problem, not a new theorem.

instances.title: Measure in twos
instances.hint: Fill A and pour into B. Think of every quantity in two-unit bundles.
instances.insight: A common factor restricts reachable amounts; a two-unit target remains reachable.
instances.prerequisites: Track amounts and free space; pours stop only at an empty source or full destination.
instances.difficulty_reasoning: A common factor restricts reachable amounts; a two-unit target remains reachable.

families.title: Odd-pebble balance
families.rules: Exactly one suspect pebble differs; all other pebbles have the same weight. Compare disjoint equal-size groups. A weighing reports left heavier, right heavier, or balance. The budget counts actual weighings. Declare only when the evidence uniquely identifies the pebble and, when required, whether it is heavy or light. A pebble marked Normal is a known genuine reference.
families.mathematics: Ternary decision trees, worst-case experimental design, information bounds, and signed hypotheses. A strategy must work on every consistent hidden state, not merely guess the chosen secret.

instances.title: The pebble off the scale
instances.prompt: One of these 3 pebbles is heavier than the others. Find it using at most 1 weighing.
instances.hint: Try one pebble on each pan. A balance is information too.
instances.insight: Three possible outcomes distinguish three locations in one weighing.
instances.readiness: Entry: distinguish a tilt from balance.

instances.title: Keep an unweighed group
instances.prompt: One of these 4 pebbles is heavier than the others. Find it using at most 2 weighings.
instances.hint: You can learn something without putting every pebble on the scale.
instances.insight: A first question need not identify the pebble immediately; preserve a solvable follow-up.

instances.title: Three groups, two questions
instances.prompt: One of these 9 pebbles is heavier than the others. Find it using at most 2 weighings.
instances.hint: Compare three with three; keep three off the scale.
instances.insight: All three outcomes must leave at most three suspects to finish in one more weighing.

instances.title: Which way is it different?
instances.prompt: One of these 3 pebbles is heavier or lighter than the others. Find it and tell which way it differs using at most 2 weighings.
instances.hint: After a tilt, a pebble on the high side may be the light one.
instances.insight: Track signed hypotheses: A-heavy and B-light can produce the same tilt.
instances.readiness: Stretch: track both identity and heavy/light status; a visible notebook helps.

instances.title: Use a trusted pebble
instances.prompt: One of these 4 pebbles is heavier or lighter than the others. Find it and tell which way it differs using at most 2 weighings. R is a known normal pebble.
instances.hint: R is normal. Use it to make a comparison that could not be made before.
instances.insight: A reference changes what experiments are possible; four unknowns now fit in two weighings.
instances.readiness: Stretch: track both identity and heavy/light status; a visible notebook helps.

instances.title: Learn which pebbles are trustworthy
instances.prompt: One of these 8 pebbles is heavier or lighter than the others. Find it and tell which way it differs using at most 3 weighings.
instances.hint: Pebbles ruled out by the first weighing can become references.
instances.insight: Switch from locating a group to distinguishing heavy-on-one-side from light-on-the-other; reuse established normal pebbles.
instances.readiness: Stretch: track both identity and heavy/light status; a visible notebook helps.

instances.title: Split into three pairs
instances.hint: Compare two pebbles against two, leaving a pair off the scale.
instances.insight: Each first outcome must leave no more than three candidates.
instances.prerequisites: Read balance outcomes; track which pebble and which direction of weight still fit.
instances.difficulty_reasoning: Each first outcome must leave no more than three candidates.
